title: Scanner results aggregation and evidence flow (runbook)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working runbook for how we aggregate vulnerability scanner outputs into canonical evidence records, enforce RBAC v2 access controls for evidence pipelines, and export normalized signals to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). It also defines the automation checks we run to verify patch application and SLA escalations.

Context / motivation:
- We currently ingest multiple scanner types (Snyk, Trivy, Dependabot, Qualys web scanner, internal binary scanner) that all emit different schemas and severities.
- Operations burden: security engineers manually reconcile duplicates, generate proof artifacts, and shepherd patches through SRE/product teams.
- Goal: reduce manual triage by normalizing outputs, auto-attaching evidence, and triggering SIEM events with consistent fields so downstream analytics and alerts work reliably.

High-level architecture (plain language):
1) Scanner collectors: per-scanner microservices pull raw reports (some push via webhooks).
2) Normalizer: converts raw findings into a canonical "evidence record" JSON (single-line per finding) and computes dedupe keys.
3) Evidence store: signed, append-only store (S3 with object versioning + KMS) holds the canonical records and proof artifacts (patch PR links, package manifests, binary hashes).
4) Access & RBAC v2: ingestion services write with service-account roles. Read access gated by RBAC v2 groups (sec-read, sec-write, eng-owner, exec-audit).
5) SIEM exporter: batch and streaming exporters map canonical fields to SIEM event fields and forward.
6) Automation engine: runs verification checks (patch deployed, config changed, CI evidence) and updates evidence status + triggers escalations per SLA.

Canonical evidence record (informal schema description) - single-line JSON per finding in object store:
- record_id: canonical-<scanner>-<hash> (dedupe key)
- first_seen: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ
- last_seen: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ
- scanner: Snyk | Trivy | Dependabot | Qualys | internal-binary
- scanner_finding_id: raw id from scanner
- severity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW | INFO (normalized from scanner)
- affected_entity: type:name (e.g., container:auth-service, repo:redwood/platform, host:i-0abcd)
- vuln_identifier: CVE-XXXX-YYYY or package-specific identifier
- evidence_artifacts: list of object paths (s3://sec-evidence/2026/11/...)
- remediation_suggested: text from scanner or curated note
- remediation_status: open | in_progress | patched | mitigated | false_positive
- assignees: list of usernames (security or eng owners)
- sla_deadline: YYYY-MM-DD (computed from severity & policy)
- proof_signatures: list of signature object paths
- notes: free text (triage comments)

Notes: the above stays as a single-line JSON string per object in the evidence store. We avoid nested objects beyond lists of strings to keep simple indexing.

Deduplication rules / heuristics (working):
- Primary dedupe key: (vuln_identifier OR package@version fingerprint) + affected_entity + normalized_path + scanner_family
- Fuzzy match: if package name and range overlap and path overlaps > 70% treat as same finding
- Merge strategy: latest first_seen, union of evidence_artifacts, highest severity prevails, combine assignees

RBAC v2 implications (practical):
- Ingestion pipeline runs under a dedicated service principal with role sec-ingest-writer. It must not have read access to evidence store except to write metadata.
- Read access is mediated by short-lived credentials minted by gateway which enforces team membership in RBAC v2 groups.
- Audit requirement: any transition of remediation_status must be logged with actor, timestamp, and justification (minimum 3 fields) against audit_log_schema v1.2.
- Escalation flows: only members of sec-oncall and eng-sre can escalate severity->pager duty. RBAC groups are mapped to these roles in the gateway config.

SIEM export mapping (fields we must guarantee for queries/alerts):
- event_type: vuln_evidence_ingest | vuln_status_change | vuln_evidence_verified
- event_time: ISO 
- evidence_id: same as record_id
- severity: normalized severity
- entity: affected_entity
- vuln_id: vuln_identifier
- status: remediation_status
- assignees: comma-separated list
- sla_deadline: ISO date
- proof_present: true|false
- dedupe_key: (used for correlation)
- ingestion_source: scanner name
- cluster/region/tags: tags from infra metadata (as CSV)

SIEM notes: Splunk expects key=value pairs; Datadog expects JSON. Our exporter supports both by serializing the canonical record into the target shape. Ensure truncated fields are avoided - proof_artifacts list should be referenced by an index URL rather than embedding long lists in Splunk events.

Automation checks (what we run after ingestion):
- check-1: repo vulnerability -> is there an open PR/Dependabot PR? If yes, attach PR link to evidence and set remediation_status=in_progress.
- check-2: host vuln -> is there a package update in system package manager? attach patch candidate and CI run link
- check-3: container image vuln -> does image digest change in prod within 7 days? if yes, mark patched and attach deployment rollout id
- check-4: web-app vuln -> has WAF rule or config mitigation been applied? attach firewall rule id and config diff
- check-5: false positive heuristics (signature-based for internal binary scanner) - annotate with confidence

Patch SLA & escalation policy (summary)
- CRITICAL: SLA 48 hours to mitigation or rollback + immediate pager if public exploit exists.
- HIGH: SLA 14 days to patch candidate or mitigation plan.
- MEDIUM: SLA 90 days.
- LOW/INFO: SLA 180 days / backlog.
Escalation steps: automated Slack alert -> owner ack within 8 hours -> if unacknowledged escalate to sec-oncall -> open exec-notify if SLA missed by 24 hours beyond escalation threshold.

Evidence automation - signatures and verification:
- When an automation job marks a finding as patched, it must attach a signed attestation (GPG or KMS-signed), stored under evidence_artifacts and referenced in proof_signatures.
- Verification job will re-scan (or query deployment state) and record a verification_result event in the evidence record; verification_result must include scan_hash and timestamp.
- Chain of custody: every state transition appends a signed log object to the evidence object store.

Operational runbook (quick steps for oncall/security engineer):
1) Open SIEM query for event_type=vuln_evidence_ingest and severity>=HIGH since last 24h.
2) For each evidence_id: review evidence_artifacts, triage note, and assignee. Use dedupe_key to collapse duplicates.
3) If remediation_status=open: add recommended assignee (eng-owner) and set sla_deadline based on severity. Post short summary to #sec-vuln-ops slack thread with link to evidence record.
4) If automation shows remediation_status=patched but proof_signatures missing -> run verification job and attach signed evidence manually if automation failed.
5) If SLA breach imminent (>75% of window elapsed) -> escalate per policy (pager -> exec-notify).

Outstanding puzzles / TODOs (working list):
- How to surface transient findings (flapping) vs persistent ones without flooding SIEM. (idea: require 2 sightings across 24h for medium/low to forward to SIEM)
- Standardize severity mapping for internal binary scanner (currently on different numeric scale).
- RBAC v2 authZ: ensure cross-account read (vendor security reviews) can be short-lived and audited.
- Evidence retention policy: propose 3 years for compliance, 90 days for quick access cache. Need legal sign-off.
- Add sample SIEM dashboards for SLA compliance and patch velocity.

Links and references (working):
- Confluence schema: CONFLUENCE-SEC/vuln-evidence-schema-2026 (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira epic: JIRA-SEC-4127 - "evidence automation pipeline"
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security-automation/pull/89
- Slack channel: #sec-vuln-ops (for alerts and triage)

Notes to self (short):
- Keep evidence record minimal and indexed; long artifacts should be referenced by URL.
- Keep RBAC checks early in the exporter to avoid accidental leaks to SIEM.
- Add a "confidence" field later to support our false positive suppression ML job.

Version history (this doc):
- 2026-11-08: initial draft by Asha K.
- 2026-11-09: added SIEM mapping and SLA table (Michael T. review)

Changelog pointer: see linked_artifacts for active tickets.

--end of runbook --
